Nested List Type-Switch Test

This document exercises a list that switches type across nesting depth: an ordered list containing a nested unordered list, and (further down) an unordered list containing a nested ordered list. The plain lists.html fixture already nests same-type lists (ul-in-ul, ol-in-ol) and flattens them into a single group with only the bullet/number marker changing per item; this fixture checks whether a type switch across the nesting boundary changes that behavior — e.g. produces a separate child group, or a different label.

Ordered containing nested unordered

  1. First ordered step
  2. Second ordered step, with a nested unordered list:
    • Nested unordered item A
    • Nested unordered item B
  3. Third ordered step

Unordered containing nested ordered

  • First unordered item
  • Second unordered item, with a nested ordered list:
    1. Nested ordered sub-step one
    2. Nested ordered sub-step two
  • Third unordered item
